title: Literary Theory
tagline: What literature is, literature and society, the creative process, the levels of a literary work, narrative, lyric, drama, genre and style, reading and interpretation, and the schools of modern theory
summary: Literary theory asks what literature is, how it is made, how a work is built and how readers make sense of it. This course introduces those questions through both the Chinese and the Western traditions: literature’s relation to society and to the writer, the levels of a literary work, the theory of narrative, lyric and drama, genre and style, the reader’s part in interpretation, and a map of the main twentieth-century schools from formalism to cultural studies.

chapters.title: What literature is
chapters.summary: Definitions of literature in China and the West, literature as an art of language, and the boundaries of the literary.

chapters.title: Literature and society
chapters.summary: Imitation and expression, literature as a reflection of life, ideology, and the market.

chapters.title: The creative process
chapters.summary: Inspiration and craft, experience and imagination, and what writers have said about how they work.

chapters.title: The levels of a literary work
chapters.summary: Language, image and meaning, from Wang Bi’s words, images and ideas to Ingarden’s strata.

chapters.title: Narrative
chapters.summary: Story and discourse, narrators and point of view, and time and plot in narrative works.

chapters.title: Lyric
chapters.summary: The lyric self, image and *yijing*, and the Chinese traditions of poetry as the expression of intent and of feeling.

chapters.title: Drama
chapters.summary: Conflict, character and action, tragedy and comedy, and Chinese opera compared with Western drama.

chapters.title: Genre and style
chapters.summary: Classifying genres, the Chinese theory of genres, and individual and period style.

chapters.title: Reading and interpretation
chapters.summary: The reader’s part, the hermeneutic circle and reception theory, and the Chinese ideas of knowing the author and meeting the author’s intent.

chapters.title: Schools of modern theory
chapters.summary: Formalism, New Criticism, structuralism, psychoanalysis, Marxist criticism, feminism, postcolonialism and cultural studies in outline.
